design.data_generating_process: two-dimensional Gaussian trait with species baseline linked to geographic centre plus a within-species local linear response vector whose orientation spans an increasing fraction of the trait-space circle

comparators: naive pooled pairwise Spearman on geographic distance vs Euclidean trait distance
equal-species matched-null omnibus of within-species geographic distance vs Euclidean trait distance
species fixed-intercept common signed multivariate response vector tested by a two-degree-of-freedom Wald statistic

interpretation.supported: Complete-row multivariate matched-null inference remains calibrated in the effect-zero cells and detects within-species trait-space organization when species response vectors differ in orientation. A common signed multivariate response vector is highly efficient when orientations are shared, but loses power when directions span the full trait-space circle and cancel in the cross-species mean. The distinction is estimand alignment, not universal superiority.
not_supported: Euclidean trait distance is optimal for every multivariate phenotype
common multivariate response models are inappropriate when species share a response direction
the observed 0.05 maximum null rejection fractions are universal type-I error guarantees
multivariate matched-null inference identifies which trait dimensions cause spatial organization
this benchmark validates arbitrary high-dimensional, nonlinear or MNAR multivariate processes
